summary: Summarizes the relationship between the IETF and the Internet Society after the 2018 restructuring into IASA 2.0. The change altered the IETF's administrative, legal, and financial structure, so this document revises RFC 2031.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 8712 explains how the IETF and Internet Society work together after the IETF's 2018 administrative restructuring. It distinguishes the IETF's responsibility for technical standards from ISOC's legal, financial, and process roles.

questions: what does isoc do for the ietf
what is the relationship between ietf and isoc
subtitle: A summary of the IETF and Internet Society relationship after the IASA 2.0 changes.

tldr.problem: The 2018 IASA 2.0 restructuring changed the IETF's administrative, legal, and financial arrangements, making the earlier summary of its relationship with ISOC outdated.
tldr.mechanism: The RFC describes the division of responsibilities: the IETF controls standards' technical content, while ISOC has limited process roles and supports the IETF LLC legally and financially.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8712 replaces RFC 2031 as a high-level summary of the IETF-ISOC relationship. It is Informational and introduces no new IANA actions or security considerations.

today: RFC 8712 replaces RFC 2031 as the high-level summary of the IETF-ISOC relationship. It is Informational, and the unit metadata lists no later RFC that obsoletes or updates it.

sections.title: Why the Relationship Was Rewritten
sections.content:
The Internet Society (ISOC) provides a corporate home for the administrative entity supporting the IETF, IAB, and IRTF. The IETF itself is primarily a volunteer organization that develops and maintains Internet Standards.

In 2018, the IASA2 Working Group revised the IETF administrative structure. One result was the creation of the IETF Administration LLC as an ISOC subsidiary. RFC 8712 summarizes the changed relationship and replaces RFC 2031.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF changed how its administration is organized in 2018. This RFC updates the description of how the IETF and ISOC relate to each other.

sections.title: Technical Responsibility and Shared Principles
sections.content:
The IETF remains responsible for developing and maintaining Internet Standards. RFC 8712 says ISOC, as an organization, has no direct influence on the technical content of those standards, though ISOC employees may contribute as individuals.

The RFC describes the organizations as philosophically aligned around open standards and multistakeholder processes. ISOC's connection with the IETF community also supports its policy work.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF decides the technical content of Internet Standards. ISOC supports the surrounding work but does not direct that technical content.

sections.title: Roles in Each Organization's Work
sections.content:
ISOC has a limited role in the IETF standards process. It appoints the IETF NomCom chair, confirms IAB candidates put forward by the NomCom, and serves as a last resort in the appeals process. ISOC also maintains relationships with other standards organizations.

The IETF appoints trustees to the ISOC Board under ISOC's bylaws. The IAB provides advice to ISOC's Board and officers on technical, architectural, procedural, and policy matters related to the Internet.
sections.plainLanguage: ISOC has specified appointment and appeal roles in the IETF process. The IETF also appoints some ISOC trustees, and the IAB advises ISOC on Internet-related matters.

sections.title: Legal Structure and the IETF Trust
sections.content:
The IETF LLC is a disregarded limited liability company of ISOC. It provides a corporate legal framework for activities related to the IETF, IAB, and IRTF and was established under an agreement dated August 27, 2018.

The IETF Trust provides legal protection for the RFC Series, trademarks, copyrights, and other intellectual-property rights. Standards documents can be freely downloaded, copied, and distributed, while the IETF retains the rights to change them. The LLC's creation changed how Trust trustees are selected but not the Trust's purpose or operation.
sections.plainLanguage: The LLC provides a legal structure for IETF-related activities. A separate trust protects the RFC Series and other IETF intellectual property.

sections.title: Funding and Administration
sections.content:
ISOC agreed to provide significant funding support for the IETF. The IETF LLC manages the annual operating budget, contracts, fundraising, bank accounts, and liability insurance.

The IETF LLC is run by a board of directors, including a director appointed by ISOC's Board of Trustees. The stated intention is for ISOC and the IETF LLC to operate at arm's length. Under IASA 2.0, the LLC is solely responsible for IETF administration.
sections.plainLanguage: ISOC provides funding, while the IETF LLC manages the budget, contracts, and administrative work. The RFC says the two are intended to operate at arm's length.
